objective: Wire the Makefile targets that CI never invoked into the workflow that already owns their checks, as separately named steps, so a failure names the check rather than the aggregate make check, and make description-check able to fail at all.
decision_supported: Does every gate this repository declares actually run in CI, and can each one report a failure that names it?
acceptance: foundation-checks runs make ready-gate as a separate named step, so a failure names the check rather than the aggregate make check.

make description-check can fail: it no longer runs generate_frames.py without --check, which rewrote a hand-edited artifact before --check compared it, so the target could not detect the condition it exists for.

make description-check is not run in foundation-checks, because expanding the model needs xacro (ros-jazzy-xacro), which that Python-only job does not have; the first CI run of this change failed there on ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'xacro'.
make description-check is instead a hard check in the container job, whose image carries ros-jazzy-xacro, via make container-description-check.

Both description tools exit 2 (INCOMPLETE) when xacro is unavailable, and make description-check reports that as a named SKIP with the reason rather than a pass, so 'could not run it' is never printed as green.

make branch-protection-check runs in a job of its own, and exit 2 is reported as a named INCOMPLETE notice with the reason and the token to set, never as a silent pass, while a readable contradiction still fails the job.

make release-commit-check is not added to every pull request, because it reads the release commit; the release workflow already runs check_release_commit.py directly before building, which is the same gate.

The branch-protection job is added to .github/rulesets/main-protection.json and to the table in docs/security/branch-protection.md in the same change, so the declaration and the enforcement cannot disagree.
Tests fail on the previous state: removing the ready-gate wiring, restoring the generator-without-check line, or moving description-check back into foundation-checks fails the suite.
Both workflow YAML files parse and every action reference stays pinned to a 40-character commit SHA.
evidence: The first CI run of this change: foundation-checks failed at 'Run make description-check' with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'xacro', which is why the step moved to the container job.
make description-check on a clean tree with xacro: PASS. On a tree with one hand-edited value in revision-d-frames.json: exit 1 naming the file as stale or hand-edited, and the file is not rewritten.

make description-check with xacro blocked: 'INCOMPLETE: cannot expand the model: No module named xacro', then 'SKIP description-check: xacro is unavailable here (INCOMPLETE, not a pass)', exit 0 with the skip recorded.
Parsed YAML showing the branch-protection job, the container-description-check step in container-full-stack, and that foundation-checks carries the ready-gate step but not description-check.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: Wiring branch-protection-check as a hard required check would make every pull request red on a permission no contributor can grant; the issue asks for a named skip with a recorded reason, and a silent pass is equally forbidden.
release-commit-check must not run on every pull request, because it reads the release commit and its required checks; the release workflow already owns that gate.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to another workflow or to a check script's logic.
description-check would have to keep regenerating the artifact in order to pass, which defeats the check rather than wiring it.
data_classification: Repository-local workflow configuration, Makefile targets and public check names. No credentials are read, written or logged; the new job reads an optional secret and never prints it.
model_policy: Deterministic Python, make and YAML only; no model inference and no external service calls added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: A required check that reports INCOMPLETE as a notice could be read as a pass. The job prints the reason and the token to set, the documentation states the outcome, and the committed declaration and page are still checked by the unit tests, so the gap is visible rather than silent.

description-check now skips in a Python-only job instead of failing, which means a hand-edited frames artifact is caught only in the container job. That is the honest split: the check cannot run without xacro, and printing a pass it did not earn would be worse than naming the skip.
description-check no longer regenerates the artifact, so a contributor who changes the description must run generate_frames.py by hand. The failure message names that command.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: remove the workflow steps and the job, restore the Makefile targets and the two tools' main functions, and drop the declaration entry.
